title: Project-Based Conversion Versus Prototype-Based Instruction in Automotive Teacher Education
text_snippet: Project-Based Conversion Versus Prototype-Based Instruction in Automotive Teacher Education The transition to electric and hydrogen mobility is reshaping the competencies that automotive vocational teaching requires, yet institutions with limited equipment must choose between authentic learning designs without evidence of what each produces. Indonesian research to date has built substitute learning media and reported feasibility ratings rather than measured learning. This study asks what cognitive and psychomotor gains two contrasting designs produce and how those gains compare. Two pre-experimental studies were conducted in one automotive teacher education programme in Indonesia. Study A used a time-series design across three project cycles of 200 minutes in which 15 undergraduates converted a combustion go-kart to electric propulsion, and Study B used a pretest-posttest design in a single 100-minute discovery session with a hydrogen fuel cell motorcycle prototype and 30 undergraduates. Achievement was measured with validated tests, observation rubrics, and response questionnaires, then analysed using normalised gain and paired samples tests. title: Analysis of Needs for Web-Based Mobile Learning Development Based on Universal Design for Learning for Students with Special Needs
text_snippet: Analysis of Needs for Web-Based Mobile Learning Development Based on Universal Design for Learning for Students with Special Needs Higher education institutions still have substantial challenges when it comes to accommodating students with special needs, especially those who are visually or aurally impaired. Access to learning resources is still an issue, as are the limitations of adaptive learning media and the dominance of more conventional verbal and visual methods of information transmission. Hence, not all pupils are given the same chances throughout the learning process. With its emphasis on providing a variety of representational, interactive, and expressive tools, Universal Design for Learning (UDL) aims to meet the requirements of students with a wide range of learning styles. In order to provide accessible learning materials for students with disabilities, this research set out to determine what was necessary to build UDL-based online mobile learning. A needs-analysis methodology was used in this qualitative investigation. Participants were chosen at random from among students who were visually impaired, students who were hearing impaired, and professionals who work with kids who had visual impairments. The data was evaluated using theme analysis after being gathered via semi-structured interviews. F

title: Evaluation of Land Suitability in the Watu Ondo Waterfall Area Using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) Method
text_snippet: Evaluation of Land Suitability in the Watu Ondo Waterfall Area Using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) Method This study was motivated by the importance of utilizing land physical conditions as a basis for developing disaster mitigation education in natural tourist areas. The study aims to evaluate land suitability for disaster mitigation education in the Watu Ondo Waterfall area using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). A quantitative research method was employed, involving AHP weighting analysis of the parameters topography, rainfall, dry season duration, soil type, and land cover, followed by spatial overlay to generate a land suitability map. The results indicate that topography is the dominant factor with a weight of 47%, followed by rainfall at 25%, soil type at 13%, dry season duration at 9%, and land cover at 5%, with a Consistency Ratio of 0.042, indicating good consistency in the assessment. Most of the area falls into the “highly suitable” (S1) and “suitable” (S2) categories, making it a potential site for disaster mitigation education based on real-world field conditions. title: Pre-Service Teachers' Experiences on Teaching Essay Writing to Grade 10 Learners in the Eastern Cape
text_snippet: Pre-Service Teachers' Experiences on Teaching Essay Writing to Grade 10 Learners in the Eastern Cape This paper explores pre-service teachers’ experiences in teaching essay writing to Grade 10 English First Additional Language learners. Despite the significance of essay writing for developing learners' writing skills in multilingual classrooms, writing essays remains a challenge for most English First Additional learners. The extant research has examined the challenges that learners face in essay writing. However, there is limited research examining pre-service teachers’ experiences in teaching essay writing during their teaching practice. This paper employed a qualitative research approach, and data were drawn from 30 pre-service teachers’ reflective journals based on their teaching practice experiences. Cognitive Process Theory was utilized as the theoretical framework for this paper. The findings included inadequate writing proficiency among learners, a lack of motivation to write, overcrowded, resource-constrained classrooms, and fear of making mistakes, all of which hinder learners’ progress in writing. The paper recommends pedagogical approaches to facilitate learners’ writing skills, additional time for creative writing, and the establishment of writing clubs in schools. Fu

title: Flipbook-Based Media to Prevent Academic Burnout among Senior High School Students in Yogyakarta
text_snippet: Flipbook-Based Media to Prevent Academic Burnout among Senior High School Students in Yogyakarta Academic burnout is a pressing issue that negatively affects senior high school students, yet conventional counseling services often rely on monotonous, static media that fail to engage today's digital generation. To address this urgent gap, this research aimed to develop an interactive digital Flipbook as a preventive intervention. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model, consisting of Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. Product validation was conducted by media experts and subject-matter experts, while the practicality test involved two Guidance and Counseling teachers. The effectiveness test was carried out through an experimental study involving 69 students from SMA Negeri 1 Pakem and SMA Negeri 1 Depok using an academic burnout scale. Data were analyzed descriptively and statistically using SPSS. The findings showed that the Flipbook media was categorized as highly feasible by both media and subject-matter experts, obtaining a validity score of 1.00. title: Improving Bench Work Competence Through QR Code Based E-LKPD Featuring SOP Video and K3 Safety Checklist
text_snippet: Improving Bench Work Competence Through QR Code Based E-LKPD Featuring SOP Video and K3 Safety Checklist This study examines the use of a QR Code-based E-LKPD integrated with SOP videos and a K3 safety checklist in improving vocational students’ bench work competence. A pretest–posttest control group design was applied to 63 tenth-grade machining students at SMKN 1 Jenangan Ponorogo in the 2025/2026 academic year selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using performance assessment observation sheets and written tests. The results show that both groups achieved the competent category, with the experimental class obtaining a slightly higher mean score (80.22) than the control class (77.07), However the independent t-test results indicate that the difference is not statistically significant (p = 0.323). Analysis of the improvement in learning outcomes also shows that the experimental class had a higher N-gain score (0.44) compared to the control class (0.39), but the difference in gain scores between the two classes was also not significant (p = 0.398). Although the difference was not statistically significant, the highest competency achievement was observed in work attitude and cleanliness, whereas the lowest achievement was found in cutting and work quality. title: Conceptual Framework of Professional Learning Communities for Cambodian Upper Secondary School Teachers
text_snippet: Conceptual Framework of Professional Learning Communities for Cambodian Upper Secondary School Teachers This paper explores the challenges of teacher professional development within Cambodian public upper secondary schools, driven by low teacher qualifications, resource gaps, and cultural barriers. Using an integrative literature review and qualitative document analysis, this paper synthesizes 58 sources, including official Cambodian regulatory frameworks, global evaluations, and empirical studies. By synthesizing local policy with international PLC models from Japan, South Korea, and Singapore, this study reveals a substantial gap between national policy goals and local school conditions. To bridge this divide, the article presents a contextually adapted four-pillar conceptual framework alongside actionable strategies to support effective PLC implementation across Cambodian upper secondary schools.

title: Digital Leadership Patterns of School Principals in Coding and Artificial Intelligence Learning
text_snippet: Digital Leadership Patterns of School Principals in Coding and Artificial Intelligence Learning Digital transformation in education requires school principals to integrate technology into learning processes and school management. This study aims to analyze principals' digital leadership patterns in supporting Coding and Artificial Intelligence learning at SMP Islam Al Azhar 26 Yogyakarta and SMP Islam Al Azhar 66 Bantul. This research employed a descriptive qualitative approach and the data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation for data collection. The participants consisted of principals, vice principals for curriculum, and teachers. The findings reveal that both schools implement transformational digital leadership through establishing a digital vision, enhancing teacher competencies, providing technological infrastructure, and strengthening digital ethics. Similarities were found in the integration of CAI learning, teacher professional development, and technological support systems. Differences were identified in length of the program, implementation strategies, and human resource management. title: Navigating Digital Transformation: Students’ and Lecturers’ Perceptions and Experiences of Online Teaching in South African Higher Education
text_snippet: Navigating Digital Transformation: Students’ and Lecturers’ Perceptions and Experiences of Online Teaching in South African Higher Education The digital transformation of higher education has reshaped teaching and learning practices, but experiences in South African universities remain diverse because of differences in technological access, digital readiness and institutional support. This systematic literature review aimed to examine students' and lecturers’ perceptions and experiences of online teaching and learning in South African tertiary institutions. The review employed studies retrieved from Google Scholar, ERIC, Scopus, and Web of Science. A total of 1253 studies from across the globe were identified and screened using Covidence, resulting in 21 South African studies meeting the inclusion criteria. The selected studies were analysed thematically to identify key patterns relating to online teaching and learning. Findings show that online learning enhances flexibility, and accessibility to educational resources. However, the review highlights the challenges, including inadequate digital infrastructure, unequal access to technology, limited digital competences, and inadequate support from institutions for both students and lecturers. title: Slang in Tiktok Videos: A Study of Linguistics and Its Implications on BIPA Informal Vocabulary Learning
text_snippet: Slang in Tiktok Videos: A Study of Linguistics and Its Implications on BIPA Informal Vocabulary Learning Mastery of informal vocabulary is one of the main challenges for Indonesian as a Foreign Language (BIPA) learners, since slang on social media. Unfortunately, contextual and relevant teaching materials that cover slang for BIPA learners are limited. This study aims to identify the linguistic forms of slang language in TikTok videos, analyze their usage, and examine their implications for informal vocabulary learning in BIPA. The present study is descriptive-analytical with a linguistic approach, including phonological, morphological, pragmatic, and semantic analyses. Data were collected through observation and documentation of TikTok videos. This study reveals two particular linguistic forms, namely phonological and morphological aspects. The use of slang is categorized into three types of illocutionary acts and three types of meaning changes. Findings from this study are expected to serve as a basis for developing informal BIPA vocabulary learning supplements based on authentic social media content.

title: CIPROPAD Learning Model to Improve Elementary School Students’ HOTs in Geometry
text_snippet: CIPROPAD Learning Model to Improve Elementary School Students’ HOTs in Geometry The latest digital technology developments demand innovative learning models that are able to integrate active learning approaches, problem-solving, and digital collaborative platforms. This study aims to develop a CIPROPAD (Circuit Learning, Problem-Based-Learning, Padlet) learning model designed to improve students' HOTS. This study uses the Borg and Gall R&D method which includes the stages of needs analysis, model design, initial product development, expert validation, limited trials, revisions, and field trials. The research subjects consisted of 74 elementary school students divided into experimental and control groups. The research instruments used included expert validation sheets, HOTS tests, student activity observation sheets, and student response questionnaires. The results of the study indicate that the CIPROPAD learning model meets the criteria of being valid, practical, and effective. Expert validation yielded an Aikens’V coeffient of 0,80 indicating highly valid. The limited implementation rate of 76%, while the student response reached 80% . title: Evaluation of Music Education Implementation Under the Merdeka Curriculum at the Junior Secondary School Level in Tanggamus Regency
text_snippet: Evaluation of Music Education Implementation Under the Merdeka Curriculum at the Junior Secondary School Level in Tanggamus Regency Music education in Indonesian junior high schools often faces persistent structural challenges, particularly in regions where the implementation of Kurikulum Merdeka remains uneven and under-evaluated. This study evaluates the implementation of Music Education under Kurikulum Merdeka at state junior high schools in Tanggamus Regency, Lampung Province. Stufflebeam's (1966) CIPP evaluation model, encompassing Context, Input, Process, and Product components, was employed within a quantitative descriptive-evaluative design. Data were collected simultaneously using three instruments: a primary questionnaire and two supplementary instruments comprising structured observation sheets and documentation analysis sheets. Respondents included 6 school principals and curriculum vice-principals, 10 Music Education teachers, and 90 ninth-grade students purposively selected from three sample schools: SMPN 1 Sumberejo, SMPN 1 Gisting, and SMPN 2 Talang Padang. Descriptive statistics were applied through mean score calculation and the Respondent Achievement Level (RAL). title: Female Resistance to Patriarchal Norms: A Study of Identity and Self-Determination in The Film Enola Holmes (2020)
text_snippet: Female Resistance to Patriarchal Norms: A Study of Identity and Self-Determination in The Film Enola Holmes (2020) This study examines the representation of women's resistance to patriarchy through identity formation and self-determination in the film Enola Holmes (2020). Set in the Victorian era, the film portrays a patriarchal society that limits women's rights, educational opportunities, and freedom to determine their own lives. This study employed a descriptive qualitative design with a grounded theory approach. The primary data were collected through repeated observation of the film, focusing on relevant scenes, dialogues, character actions, and visual elements, and were analyzed using thematic analysis interpreted through the perspectives of patriarchy and liberal feminism. The findings reveal that patriarchy is represented through the control of women's education, behavior, and life choices, particularly through the character of Mycroft Holmes and institutional practices such as the girls' finishing school. Enola's resistance is expressed through her rejection of patriarchal expectations, independent decision-making, and the construction of her own identity. title: Assessing Digital Collaborative Skills among Pre-Service Elementary Teachers: Initial Instrument Evidence and Demographic Differences
text_snippet: Assessing Digital Collaborative Skills among Pre-Service Elementary Teachers: Initial Instrument Evidence and Demographic Differences Digital collaboration skills are an important competence for prospective elementary school teachers as 21st-century learning demands the ability to use technology to work on a team, to communicate and share responsibilities, and to reflect on the learning process. This study aims to analyze evidence of the instrument initial validity, reliability, collaborative skill profile, and score differences based on the demographic characteristics of pre-service elementary teachers after participating in digital-based collaborative learning. The research uses a post-implementation evaluative quantitative approach sourced from a digital collaborative learning research design in the fourth-semester of elementary school teacher education study program at the State University of Malang. The sample consisted of two classes, totalling 60 students, selected purposively. The learning process was carried out for two months by utilizing Sipejar LMS and Google Workspace for discussion, document sharing, project completion, and group reflection. title: Gender-Based Analysis of Critical Thinking Skills Through the Problem-Based Learning Model Assisted by Instagram Greenpeaceid
text_snippet: Gender-Based Analysis of Critical Thinking Skills Through the Problem-Based Learning Model Assisted by Instagram Greenpeaceid Environmental degradation requires students to possess critical thinking skills. However, the prevalence of conventional teaching methods is considered ineffective in honing these skills. Furthermore, gender differences that influence students’ learning styles are often not adequately accommodated. This study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of the impact of the Problem-Based Learning model assisted by the Instagram account Greenpeaceid on students’ critical thinking skills based on gender. The present study employs a quasi-experimental method using a posttest-only control group design implemented as a 2×2 treatment-by-level design. Data were collected via written tests and analyzed using a Two-Way ANOVA. The results of the study show that the application of the Problem-Based Learning model has a statistically significant effect on improving students' critical thinking abilities compared to the traditional teaching methods. The results also indicate that gender also plays a significant role, as female students tend to achieve higher average scores than male students. title: Case-Based Method Encyclopedia Of Maros Pangkep Geopark Through A Community Approach In Biraeng Village
text_snippet: Case-Based Method Encyclopedia Of Maros Pangkep Geopark Through A Community Approach In Biraeng Village The 21 st-century geography learning requires the use of contextual learning resources that are based on local potential to support deep learning. However, the availability of learning media that integrates geoparks and community knowledge is still limited. Therefore, this research and development aims to produce a community-based encyclopedia using the case-based method. It aims to determine the feasibility and effectiveness of the encyclopedia as a source of geography learning. The learning media was developed by using the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, and implementation. The encyclopedia was developed using a community-based approach to ensure the accuracy of information related to the Maros-Pangkep Geopark area, particularly at the Biraeng Village. Product validation was carried out by both subject matter and media experts. The validation results showed a feasibility presentation of 72% (feasible) in terms of content, 83.3% (feasible) in terms of presentation, 87.5% (very feasible) in terms of language, and 88% (very feasible) in terms of graphics. title: Development of Differentiated Learning Assisted by Animated Content in Speaking and Writing Learning for Second Grade Elementary School Students
text_snippet: Development of Differentiated Learning Assisted by Animated Content in Speaking and Writing Learning for Second Grade Elementary School Students Speaking and writing are basic skills that play a crucial role in supporting the academic development of elementary school students. Initial observations in one elementary school indicated that learning was still uniform, did not fully address differences in student abilities, and the use of digital media was still limited. This study aimed to analyze the development process, feasibility, and effectiveness of a differentiated learning model supported by animated content in improving the speaking and writing skills of second-grade elementary school students, as well as to identify barriers faced by teachers and students in its implementation. This study used a Research and Development (R&D) approach, which included needs analysis, design, product development, expert validation, revision, limited trials, and extensive trials. The results showed that the developed learning model was considered highly feasible by the validators. The effectiveness test showed an increase in students' speaking and writing skills with a moderate increase category, both in limited trials and extensive trials. text_snippet: Analysis of Student’s Critical Thinking Skills in Science Learning : A Gender-Based Analysis The lack of studies on the development of critical thinking skills based on students' gender and the limited thinking processes demonstrated by male and female students in science classes. The purpose of this study is to analyze students' critical thinking skills in science learning: a gender-based analysis. The research sample subjects were 4th grade 107 class V students in one of the public elementary schools in the city of Surakarta. This type of research used descriptive statistics and inferential statistics to analyze the data. The novelty of this study broadens the perspective that gender differences are not a matter of superiority or weakness, but differences in cognitive strategies. The results of quantitative research data using 6 tests according to aspects of critical thinking skills according to Facione were collected by researchers and analyzed using statistical analysis. title: The Effectiveness of Canva Based Dance Learning Media in Increasing Learning Interest of Grade VIII Students
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Canva Based Dance Learning Media in Increasing Learning Interest of Grade VIII Students This study aims to test how learning dance through the digital platform Canva affects the interest of students in learning dance at SMPN 2 in Bekasi City. This study uses a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental method through a one group pretest-posttest design. The research sample includes 39 students from class VIII.G, who were chosen through purposive sampling. Data collection was carried out by distributing a learning interest questionnaire that was given before and after the treatment was applied. The intervention included using Canva based learning media for the "Tari Piring" topic. It made use of interactive presentations, visual worksheets, and interactive quizzes, all supported by Canva AI. The analysis technique includes validity tests, reliability tests, descriptive statistics, normality testing using the Shapiro-Wilk test, and paired t-tests using SPSS. title: The Effectiveness of School-Based Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Programs
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of School-Based Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Programs Bullying and cyberbullying are increasingly complex forms of peer violence because they occur simultaneously in school spaces and digital environments. This situation demands the development of school-based prevention programs that not only target conventional bullying but also integrate cyberbullying prevention strategies. This article aims to examine the effectiveness of school-based bullying and cyberbullying prevention programs in the context of a high-performing education system. This study uses a systematic literature review design with reference to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The literature search was conducted through the Scopus database using keywords representing three main concepts: cyberbullying, bullying, and prevention or intervention programs. Of the 657 identified documents, a screening process based on publication year, document type, language, school-age population, and program focus resulted in 12 articles that met the inclusion criteria. title: The Effectiveness of Using AI as a Digital Assistant in Problem-Based Learning on Student Learning Outcomes
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of Using AI as a Digital Assistant in Problem-Based Learning on Student Learning Outcomes This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based Digital Assistant in the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model on the learning outcomes of PTI Study Program students in the mobile Programming course. The research method uses a quasi-experimental approach with a pretest-posttest control group. The results showed a significant difference between the experimental and control classes with a p value = 0.001

title: Kesiapan dan Motivasi Mahasiswa dalam Mengikuti Pembelajaran Online di Masa Pandemi COVID-19
text_snippet: Kesiapan dan Motivasi Mahasiswa dalam Mengikuti Pembelajaran Online di Masa Pandemi COVID-19 This study aimed to determine online learning readiness, motivation, and challenges for students in Indonesia during the COVID-19 pandemic. Aspects considered in this study included supporting devices and skills to use them, independence in learning, self-control for successful learning, learning motivation, and online communication. The study was conducted using an online questionnaire and crosstabs analysis. The results showed that the students had a good readiness and motivation to do online learning during the pandemic. The most common obstacles included internet connection, limited data quota, unsupported devices, and lecturer learning methods.

title: Developing Scientific Article Writing Materials Using a Hybrid Learning Approach: Insights from an Indonesian Language for Foreign Speakers (BIPA) Program
text_snippet: Developing Scientific Article Writing Materials Using a Hybrid Learning Approach: Insights from an Indonesian Language for Foreign Speakers (BIPA) Program This study aims to develop learning materials for writing scientific articles for international students using the hybrid learning approach. This approach was chosen by utilizing the advantages of offline classes combined with online classes. This approach is in accordance with the characteristics of students as millennials. For product development, we used a method consisting of product design, product design, production, and product testing. In the end, we produced learning materials to write scientific articles packaged in the form of a module of writing process-genre-based scientific articles with a hybrid learning approach for international students. title: The Relationship between Synchronous Online Training Preference and Online Student Engagements
text_snippet: The Relationship between Synchronous Online Training Preference and Online Student Engagements Online training during the pandemic was commonly held using the synchronous learning method. The aim of this study was to explore the relationship between synchronous online training preference, gender difference, and online student engagements (OSE). This study was analyzed with Structural Equation Model (SEM) by using SmartPLS 3 software. The participants of this study involved 35 online training participants and produced the following findings (1) synchronous online training preference has a positive relationship with OSE variables, (2) The relationship between OSE variables is positive, (3) a gender has a positive relationship with skills, participation, and performance, while gender has a negative relationship with emotions and synchronous online training preference.

title: Mapping Arabic Calligraphy Education Research Structure: A Bibliometric Analysis between 2016 and 2021 Using Vosviewer
text_snippet: Mapping Arabic Calligraphy Education Research Structure: A Bibliometric Analysis between 2016 and 2021 Using Vosviewer The purpose of this study is to present a bibliometric analysis of Arabic calligraphy research from the Scopus database from 2016 to 2021. This study identified 43 English documents for further analysis based on the query used and the document screening stages. In this study, Vosviewer was used to visualize the data, and Harzing's Publish or Perish is used to harvest data, calculate metrics, and analyze citations. According to our findings, Arabic calligraphy research publications are increasing, with the peak occurring in 2019, including in terms of citations. The findings indicate that research in language and arts is closely related to the primary research domain, and that the arts have the prospect to displace the language groups that previously dominated. Apart from the current subject, research into the role of language and art (aesthetics) in Arabic calligraphy is still constricted and should be expanded.

journal_name: Jurnal Pendidikan: Teori, Penelitian, dan Pengembangan
title: The Applicability of a Scale on Self-Regulated Writing Strategies in English for High School Students
text_snippet: The Applicability of a Scale on Self-Regulated Writing Strategies in English for High School Students Writing appeared to be crucial in learning foreign languages. This study aimed at examining the applicability of a measure on self-regulated writing strategies in terms of its psychometric properties. The scale items were designed from theoretical foundations and previous relevant studies. Questionnaires were distributed online to high school students, collected and analyzed as many as 106. Correlation, confirmatory factor analyses, and calculating Cronbach’s alpha were carried out to make sure the applicability of the scale. The findings showed five main constructs to be applicable. They were self-initiating, planning, text-generating, revising, and acting on feedback.

title: The Effect of Technological Literacy, Learning Facility, and Family Environment on Students’ Learning Motivation
text_snippet: The Effect of Technological Literacy, Learning Facility, and Family Environment on Students’ Learning Motivation Student achievement is influenced by a variety of factors, both internal and external, such as school and home amenities. This study intends to assess the effect of technological literacy, amenities and learning environment on the learning motivation of SMK students during the pandemic. This is a quantitative Expos-Fact style of study. This study's population and sample consisted of 58 students majoring in Automation and Office Governance at SMK PGRI Turen; questionnaires and observations were used to collect data. Multiple linear regression test was employed for data analysis. The analysis reveals that technical literacy has a favorable influence on learning motivation, that facilities have a positive effect on learning motivation, and that the learning environment has no effect on learning motivation. The environmental impact is not attributable to the fact that a lack of suitable facilities at home is not a motivating factor for student learning.

title: Development and Preliminary Effectiveness of SEL-Based Puzzle Media for Improving Emotional Regulation in Second-Grade Elementary Students
text_snippet: Development and Preliminary Effectiveness of SEL-Based Puzzle Media for Improving Emotional Regulation in Second-Grade Elementary Students This study developed and evaluated the feasibility, practicality, and preliminary effectiveness of the Social Emotional Learning (SEL)-based Puzzle Expression Emotion media to improve emotional regulation among second-grade elementary school students. The study used a Research and Development design following the ADDIE model. Feasibility was assessed by subject-matter and media experts, practicality by classroom teachers, and preliminary effectiveness through a one-group pretest-posttest field trial involving 51 students from two public elementary schools in Surakarta. Data were collected through interviews, observations, validation sheets, practicality questionnaires, and an emotional regulation instrument. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, followed by a paired-sample t-test and N-gain analysis. The results showed that the media obtained 88.33% from the media expert and 90% from the subject-matter expert, indicating high feasibility. title: Analysis of the Relationships between Students' Memory Ability and Cognitive Ability on Chemical Nomenclature
text_snippet: Analysis of the Relationships between Students' Memory Ability and Cognitive Ability on Chemical Nomenclature Memory ability was needed thing that important to research in relationships and teachers’ effort in increasing learning quality. The research aimed at knowing the correlation between students’ memory ability and cognitive ability at Islamic Senior High School of Al-Ihsan Boarding School Kubang Raya, Kampar. title: Descriptive Analysis of Career Planning and Industry Insight (Cognitive Component) among Final-Year Mechanical Engineering Education Students
text_snippet: Descriptive Analysis of Career Planning and Industry Insight (Cognitive Component) among Final-Year Mechanical Engineering Education Students This study aims to analyze the level of understanding of final-year Mechanical Engineering Education students regarding career planning and industry insight as cognitive components in preparing for the workforce. The study employed a quantitative approach with a descriptive method involving 58 eighth-semester students who had completed industrial internships. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire consisting of 20 items on career planning and 18 items on industry insight, and were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including mean scores and percentages. The results indicate that students’ understanding of career planning falls into the high category, with a mean score of 3.78, while their understanding of industry insight is also categorized as high, with a mean score of 3.52. The predominance of responses in the “agree” category suggests that students have developed an initial awareness of the importance of understanding self-potential, job opportunities, and the characteristics of the industrial world. title: A Descriptive Analysis of AI Competence and Teaching Performance among Pre-Service Automotive Engineering Teachers in Vehicle Diagnostic Learning
text_snippet: A Descriptive Analysis of AI Competence and Teaching Performance among Pre-Service Automotive Engineering Teachers in Vehicle Diagnostic Learning The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the automotive industry, particularly in vehicle diagnostics, which increasingly relies on data-driven and intelligent systems. This shift necessitates that students in Automotive Engineering Education not only possess technical skills but also demonstrate AI competence and effective teaching performance. This study aims to analyze the level of AI competence and teaching performance among students in the context of vehicle diagnostic learning. A descriptive survey research design was employed involving 87 students as respondents. Data were collected using structured questionnaires measuring dimensions of AI competence (AI literacy, AI tool utilization, AI-based problem solving, and AI integration) and teaching performance (lesson planning, instructional delivery, classroom interaction, technology use, and learning evaluation). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including mean, percentage, standard deviation, and score categorization. title: An Analysis of Web-Based Languange Learning On Students Speaking Anxiety
text_snippet: An Analysis of Web-Based Languange Learning On Students Speaking Anxiety This study explores the use of Duolingo as a web-based language learning tool and its influence on students’ speaking anxiety at MTs Nurul Falah Kota Jambi. Speaking anxiety remains a significant affective barrier in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning, particularly in traditional classroom settings where students often experience communication apprehension, fear of negative evaluation, and test anxiety. Employing a qualitative case study design, this research involved approximately 15 students who had used Duolingo for at least six weeks, along with one English teacher for triangulation. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations and analyzed using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s framework, guided by Krashen’s Affective Filter Hypothesis and the Foreign Language Classroom Anxiety Scale (FLCAS). The findings indicate that Duolingo provides a flexible, private, and engaging learning environment through gamification, speech recognition feedback, and self-paced practice, which helps reduce psychological pressure and increase students’ confidence in speaking. title: Teaching IsiXhosa as a First Additional Language in Former Model C Schools: Implications for Educator Experiences in the Harry Gwala District, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
text_snippet: Teaching IsiXhosa as a First Additional Language in Former Model C Schools: Implications for Educator Experiences in the Harry Gwala District, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa This paper explored educators' experiences of teaching isiXhosa as First Additional Language (FAL) in former Model C schools in the Harry Gwala District, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The study aimed to understand practical teaching approaches that enhance linguistic diversity and improve IsiXhosa proficiency while addressing systemic challenges. A qualitative case study design was employed, using semi-structured interviews with five IsiXhosa FAL teachers across three schools. The findings revealed the need for partnerships between schools and communities, curriculum revision, including mentorship and professional development for teachers, collaborative learning, and the effective use of technology. However, challenges such as unequal language recognition, insufficient resources, and a lack of parental and administrative support hindered effective implementation. The study recommends teacher mentorship, increased resource allocation, enhanced parental involvement, and policy reforms to promote equitable language education. title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Adaptive Learning Strategies among Deaf Students in Inclusive Higher Education: A Thematic Analysis
text_snippet: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Adaptive Learning Strategies among Deaf Students in Inclusive Higher Education: A Thematic Analysis This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of learning adaptation strategies implemented by students with hearing impairments in the context of inclusive higher education. The study employs a qualitative approach using an open-ended survey design involving 15 students with hearing impairments who are currently enrolled in or have previously attended higher education institutions. Data were analyzed using a reflexive thematic analysis approach to identify thematic patterns related to perceptions of the effectiveness of the adaptation strategies employed. The findings indicate that the majority of respondents perceived the adaptation strategies they used as “fairly effective,” although not yet fully optimal. The dominant strategies included sitting in the front rows, lip-reading, utilizing written materials and presentation slides, using transcription tools or digital devices, and engaging in discussions with peers after lectures. The findings also indicate a reliance on informal peer support and a high individual adaptation burden borne by the students. title: The Design of Chatbot Learning Media for Arabic Vocabulary Learning for 7th Grade Students at MTsN
text_snippet: The Design of Chatbot Learning Media for Arabic Vocabulary Learning for 7th Grade Students at MTsN Arabic language learning at the Madrasah Tsanawiyah (MTsN) level often faces challenges such as limited curriculum time allocation and the dominance of conventional teacher-centered methods. This research aims to produce a design for chatbot-based learning media using the Smojo.Ai platform, focusing on vocabulary (mufradat) mastery for 7th-grade students. The approach used is Research and Development (R&D) with the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation); however, this report is limited to the Design and Development (expert validation) stages. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, documentation studies, and validation questionnaires. The results indicate that the characteristics of the "Mufrodaty" chatbot integrate vocabulary material in the form of text, visual imagery, and audio, complemented by Wordwall gamification features and motivational videos. Based on the validation results from content experts, language experts, and media experts, this product obtained an average score of 98%, categorized as "Highly Feasible." title: Implementation Of Differentation Learning Based On VARK Learning Styles To Improve Dance Element Learning Outcomes Of Grade VII Students
text_snippet: Implementation Of Differentation Learning Based On VARK Learning Styles To Improve Dance Element Learning Outcomes Of Grade VII Students The low learning outcomes of grade VII students in the three domains in learning dance elements are one of them due to the dominance of conventional methods. This type of research is Kemmis and McTaggart Class Action Research (CAR) which consists of planning, implementation of actions, observation, and reflection. The research ran for two cycles with the subjects of grade VII students of SMPN 14 Bandung City for the 2025/2026 school year. Data collection techniques through observation and learning outcome tests. Data analysis used descriptive statistics in the form of average values and classical completeness. The application of VARK-based differentiation learning was proven to increase cognitive classical completeness from 47.06% to 91.17%, affective from 20.59% to 88.23% and psychomotor from 14.70% to 85.29% exceeding the success indicator of 85% in cycle II.

title: Deferred Action Theory as a Framework for Adaptive Educational Procurement: Navigating Uncertainty and Digital Transformation in Education Systems
text_snippet: Deferred Action Theory as a Framework for Adaptive Educational Procurement: Navigating Uncertainty and Digital Transformation in Education Systems Public procurement constitutes a significant portion of national expenditure and directly affects economic growth, service delivery, and governance quality. In Indonesia, education sector procurement absorbs more than half of the allocated budget but remains vulnerable to inefficiencies, rigid procedures, and corruption risks. This study aims to conceptualize an adaptive framework for Public Procurement Business Process Management (PP-BPM) that addresses environmental uncertainty, digital transformation, and governance challenges. This conceptual study integrates Deferred Action Theory (DAT), Emergent Business Processes (EBP), and Business Process Management (BPM) to develop a multi-level framework for procurement. The analysis covers strategic, managerial, and operational dimensions, emphasizing deferment points, adaptability, and complex adaptive systems (CAS) thinking. The framework demonstrates that traditional planned procurement systems are insufficient to manage non-standardizable and dynamic processes. Subjek penelitian terdiri dari 21 siswa pada uji terbatas, 30 siswa pada uji luas, dan 60 siswa pada uji efektivitas. title: Multimodal Construction of Ideational Meaning on Opening Pages of English Textbooks in China
text_snippet: Multimodal Construction of Ideational Meaning on Opening Pages of English Textbooks in China This study aims to examine how ideational meaning is multimodally constructed on 31 opening pages through the interaction of theme images and Look and Share questions in four newly published junior high school English textbooks by People’s Education Press. Adopting the multimodal discourse analytic approach, the study analyzed representational processes in 32 images using Visual Grammar and ideational processes in 97 verbal interrogatives through transitivity patterns. The findings show that opening page images are predominantly narrative, frequently foregrounding action and reactional processes. The verbal questions, in contrast, show a strong tendency toward mental processes, while material and relational processes also appear. Analysis of the interaction between visual and verbal modes reveals recurrent yet flexible patterns of alignment: reactional images often correspond with mental prompts, whereas conceptual representations tend to align with relational orientations. Overall, the study highlights opening pages as multimodal entry points where visual and verbal resources jointly shape experiential meaning at the beginning of textbook units.
